stem: Explain **two** benefits to a business of giving induction training to new employees.

So fewer accidents / legal problems.
New employees settle in and know procedures quickly.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Induction teaches new employees the safety rules at once, reducing accidents. It also helps them settle in and learn procedures quickly, so they become productive sooner and are less likely to leave in their first weeks.

explanation: Induction reduces accidents and early labour turnover and speeds up productivity.

stem: Tendai owns a small printing business in Gweru with eight employees. He has bought a new digital printing press. Only Tendai has used one before. The supplier offers a five-day course in Johannesburg for two employees, with fees, travel and accommodation to pay. Tendai's profits are low this year.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What type of training is the supplier's course?

options.content: On-the-job
options.rationale: The trainees would not be at their workplace.

options.content: Induction
options.rationale: The employees are not new.

options.content: Job rotation
options.rationale: Job rotation is a motivation method.

options.content: Off-the-job
options.rationale: Correct: it is away from the workplace.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **one** advantage of training the employees on the job instead.

points.description: Cheaper: no fees, travel or accommodation.
Tendai already knows the press, so he can train them.
Matters because profits are low this year / training on the actual press.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: On-the-job training would avoid fees, travel and accommodation costs, which matters because profits are low. Tendai has used this type of press, so he can train staff on the actual machine.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend which type of training Tendai should use. Justify your answer.

points.description: Off-the-job: expert trainers, full use of the press's features, less risk of costly mistakes.
Off-the-job: costly, staff away for five days, low profits.
On-the-job: cheap, specific to the press.
On-the-job: Tendai's own time and output lost; he may not know all features; mistakes waste paper and ink.
Possible compromise: send one employee, who then trains others on the job.
Justified recommendation.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The supplier's course would give expert training on all the press's features, reducing wasted materials, but fees, travel and five days away are expensive while profits are low. On-the-job training by Tendai is cheaper and uses the actual press, but takes his time away from running the business and he may not know every feature. I recommend sending one employee on the course, who can then train the others on the job with Tendai's help. This halves the cost while bringing expert knowledge into the business.

explanation: Expert off-the-job training is costly; a combination may give expertise at lower cost.
hints: (a) Where does the course take place?
(c) Consider low profits and the need to use the press well.

stem: A fictional hotel group is opening a new hotel in Victoria Falls and will recruit 60 staff, most with no hotel experience. The manager plans to give them a short tour on the first day and then let them learn from the few experienced staff transferred from the group's Harare hotel. Customer reviews are very important to the hotel's success.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State **two** things that should be covered in the new staff's induction training.

points.description: Health and safety / fire procedures.
Rules, hours and pay / introductions to colleagues and supervisors / layout / the hotel's standards of service.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** problems with the manager's plan to rely on on-the-job training.

points.description: Few experienced staff for 60 trainees.
Experienced staff's own work suffers / trainees get little attention.
Trainees learn on real guests.
Mistakes lead to poor reviews / bad habits passed on.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There are only a few experienced staff to train 60 people, so trainees will get little attention and the experienced staff's own work will suffer. Trainees will also learn while serving real guests, so their mistakes may lead to poor reviews, which matter greatly to the hotel.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Evaluate how the hotel should train its new staff before and after opening.

points.description: Full induction (not just a tour): safety, standards, rules.
Off-the-job training before opening (training room / college / trainers) on service skills.
Cost of training before any revenue is earned.
Benefit: good service from day one protects reviews and future bookings.
On-the-job coaching after opening by experienced staff for business-specific routines.
Justified conclusion.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The hotel should give a proper induction covering safety, rules and service standards, not just a tour. Because most staff have no experience and reviews matter, it should run off-the-job training before opening, using trainers or a hospitality college, so staff practise service skills without real guests. This costs money before any revenue is earned, but poor reviews in the first months could damage bookings for years. After opening, experienced staff can coach new staff on the job in the hotel's own routines. This combination costs more at first but protects the hotel's reputation.

explanation: Inexperienced staff in a reputation-sensitive business need induction and off-the-job training before facing customers.
hints: (b) How many trainers are there for 60 people?
